Subject: Follow-up: Access controls & support access (RBAC, break-glass)

Hi Alice — great conversation today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and next steps around the access controls topics we discussed (PII/data handling follow-up):

Recap (what we heard)
- Customer data contains PII fields for transactions and KYC; needs strict access controls and auditing.
- You want least-privilege RBAC for both API and Console access, with role definitions derived from your internal AD groups.
- Support access: you accept time-limited, auditable break-glass for Redwood support, with pre-approved escalation owners.
- Audit logs: 13–25 months retention for auth and access logs; full request/response logs retained per environment.
- Data residency: primary region US (us-east-1) with no cross-region backups for sensitive datasets.

Requested artifacts / next steps (what Marissa/Redwood will provide)
1) Access controls overview PDF (attached) — maps our RBAC model to your roles and the supported admin workflow.
2) SOC 2 summary (attached) and available evidence checklist for procurement.
3) Access controls matrix (we'll send a template) for you to map FinTrust roles to Redwood roles.
4) Proposed runbook for break-glass procedures and time-limited support tokens (we have a draft).

Questions for you
- Can you confirm the retention window requirement for auth/access logs (13 months OK, or do you need 24 months)?
- Who on your side will be the break-glass approver(s)? (name + email)
- Will you require VPC-only private deployment for regulated workloads or is a dedicated-cloud tenancy acceptable?

Attachments: redwood-access-controls-overview.pdf, SOC2_Summary.pdf

Proposed next step: technical call with Vivek (product/infra) and Dev (security/ops) — we can do Tue 2027-05-16 10:00 AM PT. Are you available?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: we need 24 months for auth/access logs; 13 months is not sufficient given our audit policy.
- Break-glass approvers: myself (alice.chen@fintrust.com) and Raj Patel (raj.patel@fintrust.com). Approvals need to be recorded and attached to the incident ticket.
- Deployment: for initial pilot, dedicated-cloud tenancy is acceptable; production for PII workloads will require VPC/private deployment.

I've attached a short doc with our access requirements and current role mappings: FinTrust-Access-Requirements.docx. It includes examples of roles that must be mapped (Compliance, QA, Support, Engineering, Third-party integrations).

We can do Tue 2027-05-16 10:00 AM PT for the call — please send a calendar invite. Also can you confirm the scope of 'support access' (console only vs. full API access) and whether support sessions are recorded and auditable?

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick responses and the doc (attached). A few clarifications and the attachments we promised: 

1) Retention: we can support 24 months retention for auth/access logs for your dedicated/private deployment. We also provide export hooks to S3/Cloud Logging for long-term archival.

2) Support access scope: Redwood support can be scoped to Console-only or Console+API. All support sessions are time-limited, tokenized, and recorded. We persist an audit trail for each session (who, when, which resources, and the session recording metadata). We can push session metadata to your SIEM via webhook.

3) Break-glass: our standard runbook is time-limited access tokens, approved by named approvers (we log approver, timestamp, justification). We also support emergency OOB approval via signed email if your incident process requires it.

4) Deployment: pilot on dedicated-cloud (your preference) -> production on VPC/private. We will provide an onboarding checklist for the VPC cutover.

Attachments included in this message: access_controls_matrix.xlsx (template), runbook-break-glass.md (runbook draft)

Proposed next steps:
- Technical call Tue 2027-05-16 10:00 AM PT (Vivek + Dev to join) — calendar invite to follow.
- FinTrust: fill the access_controls_matrix.xlsx with role mappings and highlight any third-party automated integrations.
- Redwood (Vivek/Dev): produce an annotated runbook and SOC2 evidence checklist by EOD 2027-05-14.

If that timeline works I'll move to schedule the call.

Thanks,
Marissa
